evidence: Probe judge_step_cpu.py: Transformer(judge_train_config().shape, 4096), one forward+backward at 128x256 on the CPU: 74.3 s, peak 10,754 MB RSS (558 MB before). Code read of device.py, cli.py and trainer.py.
fix: At the start of build-judge, train and bench, print the device in plain words ('training on the GPU (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050)' or 'no usable GPU found: training on the CPU'). For build-judge (and gate), refuse to fall back to the CPU unless --device cpu is given, saying it would take days.

scenario: If CUDA becomes unavailable (a driver update breaking the cu130 wheel, a CPU-only torch resolved) and the owner runs `airace-ml build-judge` without --device, pick_device() returns cpu without saying so; only the gate announces the device (gate.py:1264). The judge then trains 8x384x256 at batch 128 in fp32 with SDPA's math path storing TxT attention matrices: one measured step took 74 s and peaked at 10.75 GB RSS. The run is 3,662 steps, so roughly 1.5-3 days at about 11 GB of RAM, while the owner expects '~1 h GPU' and sees only 'step 1/3662' lines. The same silent fallback hits the gate (see the run-overwrite finding). Task 1 showed CUDA available on the owner's setup, so this happens only if that changes.
title: build-judge and train silently fall back to the CPU when CUDA is unavailable; on the CPU the judge needs about 10.7 GB of RAM per step and takes days

evidence: Probe probe3.py: 'ctx=256 batch_tokens=100 budget=1000: steps=10 tokens=2560 ratio=2.56', 'ctx=192 batch_tokens=1000 budget=4000: tokens=3840 ratio=0.96'. Hand computation for every ctx multiple of 64 up to 1024; checked experiments/configs.py and evals/judge.py:129-134.
fix: In validate(), reject batch_tokens < ctx_len (ideally require batch_tokens % ctx_len == 0). Derive steps from the real tokens per step (steps = max(1, token_budget // (batch_size*ctx_len))), or document that the budget is approximate so M3 charges compute for tokens actually trained.
line: 170-176 (steps = token_budget // batch_tokens; batch_size = max(1, batch_tokens // ctx_len)), 196-204 (validate); trainer.py:432 (tokens_per_step)
scenario: Each step trains batch_size*ctx_len tokens, not batch_tokens. A JSON config with ctx_len=256, batch_tokens=100, token_budget=1000 passes validate() and trains 10 x 256 = 2560 tokens (2.56x); ctx 1024 with batch_tokens 512 trains 2x. That breaks R3 (compute tied to the in-game budget) for configs arriving as JSON. With the default batch_tokens=16384, attention spans that do not divide it train 1.6-6% less than budgeted (ctx 384: 42 rows, 98.4%; 640: 97.7%; 832: 96.5%). Reported tokens stay honest. M1 gate and judge shapes divide their batch_tokens, so this is latent until 'Attention span' and 'Training length' become player controls.
title: Tokens actually trained per step differ from batch_tokens; validate() accepts batch_tokens < ctx_len, which trains up to 2-2.56x the paid token budget

evidence: probe2.py: tok.encode('a\ud800b') raises TypeError; validate() accepts a surrogate notebook. probe5.py: train_run with probe_prompts ['hi \ud83d'] raised TypeError at tokenizer.py:65 with telemetry.jsonl already written.
fix: In validate(), reject any notebook/coaching/probe_prompts string that does not round-trip str.encode('utf-8'), raising ValueError naming the field. Encode the probe prompts once in _prepare so nothing is first tokenized mid-run.
line: 229-241 (only isinstance(str) checks); trainer.py:203-211 (_custom_docs), 551-561 (_evaluate encodes probe prompts mid-run); tokenizer.py:65
scenario: "probe_prompts": ["hi \ud83d"] is valid JSON (JS JSON.stringify emits it for a half-pasted emoji). from_json and validate() accept it; train_run creates out_dir and telemetry.jsonl, trains to the first eval step (step 183 for a judge-sized run), then dies with 'TypeError: TextInputSequence must be str'. That is not a ValueError, so _cmd_train shows a traceback, and with no checkpoint before the first save every rerun repeats the training and crashes at the same step. The same surrogate in notebook/coaching fails in _prepare with TypeError. This breaks validate()'s contract ('nothing but a ValueError may escape for a malformed config') and train_run's claim that everything is checked before out_dir is touched.
title: Lone UTF-16 surrogates in notebook, coaching or probe_prompts pass validate() but crash the tokenizer with TypeError; a bad probe prompt only fails mid-run at the first eval, every time
